div.div: Information Nexus for investigating telemetry quality evidence across structure, consistency, CIM alignment, parsing, cardinality and duplication.

panel.title: Data Quality Summary by Data Source

div.p: What this shows: Per-source quality indicators for structure, consistency, CIM alignment, parsing fill, cardinality pressure and duplication.
How to use it: Sort by the weakest dimension or issue count to prioritise engineering review.
Read it as: These are telemetry quality indicators, not compliance or governance scores.

search.query: | eval is_meta_field=if(match(field_name,"^(host|source|sourcetype|index|splunk_server|splunk_server_group|linecount|punct|eventtype|tag)$"),1,0) | eval fill_pct=if(is_meta_field=0 AND consistency_score max(duplicate_pct) as duplicate_pct max(cardinality_score) as cardinality_score max(cardinality_pressure) as cardinality_pressure avg(fill_pct) as parsing_quality_pct max(event_count) as event_count dc(eval(if(model_has_evidence=1 AND datamodel!="__none__",field_name,null()))) as total_scope_fields dc(eval(if(model_has_evidence=1 AND matched_scope=1 AND datamodel!="__none__",field_name,null()))) as matched_scope_fields dc(eval(if(model_has_evidence=1 AND datamodel!="__none__",datamodel,null()))) as models_with_evidence by group_value | eval parsing_quality_pct=round(coalesce(parsing_quality_pct,0),0) | eval cardinality_pressure_pct=round(coalesce(cardinality_pressure,0)*100,1) | eval div.p: What this shows: Per-source cardinality pressure from distinct event shapes, hosts and sources relative to sample size.
How to use it: Sort by Cardinality score or Dominant Driver to find sources that may be expensive to search, accelerate or normalise.
Read it as: A low score means high uniqueness per event. Ask whether host/path sprawl or unstable event shapes are expected for that source.

search.query: | stats max(cardinality_score) as cardinality_score max(cardinality_pressure) as cardinality_pressure max(distinct_shapes) as distinct_shapes max(distinct_hosts) as distinct_hosts max(distinct_sources) as distinct_sources max(shape_ratio) as shape_ratio max(host_ratio) as host_ratio max(source_ratio) as source_ratio max(event_count) as event_count by group_value | eval pressure_pct=round(coalesce(cardinality_pressure,0)*100,1) | eval shape_pct=round(coalesce(shape_ratio,0)*100,1) | eval host_pct=round(coalesce(host_ratio,0)*100,1) | eval source_pct=round(coalesce(source_ratio,0)*100,1) | eval dominant_driver=case( shape_ratio>=host_ratio AND shape_ratio>=source_ratio,"Shapes", host_ratio>=source_ratio,"Hosts", true(),"Sources" ) | sort cardinality_score | rename group_value as "Data Source" | rename cardinality_score as "Cardinality" | rename pressure_pct as "Pressure %" | rename dominant_driver as "Dominant Driver" | rename distinct_shapes as "Distinct Shapes" | rename distinct_hosts as "Distinct Hosts" | rename distinct_sources as "Distinct Sources" | rename shape_pct as "Shape %" | rename host_pct as "Host %" | rename source_pct as "Source %" | rename event_count as "Events Sampled" | table "Data Source" Cardinality "Pressure %" "Dominant Driver" "Distinct Shapes" "Distinct Hosts" "Distinct Sources" "Shape %" "Host %" "Source %" "Events Sampled"

div.p: What this shows: Per-source share of events whose raw payload is repeated in the sample (md5(_raw)).
How to use it: Sort by Duplication % to spot replay, double-shipping or naturally identical heartbeats.
Read it as: High duplication is a question, not proof of a fault. Identical status events can be normal; unexpected repeats usually deserve collection review.

search.query: | stats max(duplicate_pct) as duplicate_pct max(unique_raws) as unique_raws max(event_count) as event_count by group_value | eval duplicate_events=max(event_count-unique_raws,0) | eval duplication_band=case(duplicate_pct<5,"Low",duplicate_pct<20,"Watch",true(),"High") | sort - duplicate_pct | rename group_value as "Data Source" | rename duplication_band as "Band" | rename duplicate_pct as "Duplication %" | rename unique_raws as "Unique Raws" | rename duplicate_events as "Duplicate Events" | rename event_count as "Events Sampled" | table "Data Source" Band "Duplication %" "Unique Raws" "Duplicate Events" "Events Sampled"

div.p: What this shows: Specific quality concerns raised by the scoring dimensions.
How to use it: Use this as the work queue for parsing, CIM field coverage, cardinality, or duplication investigation.
Read it as: These are evidence-led indicators. They should start the engineering conversation rather than act as automated remediation instructions.

div.p: What this shows: Per-source Field-scope coverage for datamodels that already have field evidence in the sample.
How to use it: Use this for a quick CIM breakdown on Quality IN. For tags, missing fields and perspective detail, use Data Readiness IN.
Read it as: Same CIM story as the Dimensions tile (honours the Field scope control).

search.query: | where model_field=1 | eval datamodels=if(isnull(datamodels),"__none__",datamodels) | mvexpand datamodels | rename datamodels as datamodel | where datamodel!="__none__" | stats dc(field_name) as matched_scope_fields max(event_count) as event_count by group_value datamodel | join type=left max=0 datamodel [ | inputlookup datamodel_fields_lookup | eval datamodel=trim(datamodel) | eval field_name=lower(trim(field_name)) | eval recommended=if(recommended="true" OR recommended=1,1,0) | eval required=if(required="true" OR required=1,1,0) | eval scope_field=case( "$field_scope$"="all",1, "$field_scope$"="recommended" AND (recommended=1 OR required=1),1, true(),0 ) | where scope_field=1 | stats dc(field_name) as total_scope_fields by datamodel ] | eval cim_alignment_pct=round(if(total_scope_fields>0,(matched_scope_fields/total_scope_fields)*100,0),0) | rename group_value as "Data Source" | rename datamodel as "Datamodel" | rename matched_scope_fields as "Matched Recommended Fields" | rename total_scope_fields as "Total Recommended Fields" | rename cim_alignment_pct as "CIM Alignment %" | rename event_count as "Events Sampled" | table "Data Source" Datamodel "CIM Alignment %" "Matched Recommended Fields" "Total Recommended Fields" "Events Sampled" | sort "Data Source" - "CIM Alignment %" Datamodel
